text:
The University of Melbourne is a leading Australian research university established in 1853, located primarily in Parkville, Melbourne. It has a diverse range of campuses including Southbank, Burnley, Werribee, and a planned Fishermans Bend campus. The university is structured into nine faculties, including Arts, Business and Economics, Engineering and Information Technology, Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences, Science, Law, Architecture, Building and Planning, and Fine Arts and Music.
The university is known for its "Melbourne Model" undergraduate curriculum, which replaced traditional specialist degrees with generalist degrees followed by professional or research graduate courses. This model, introduced in 2008, has been controversial due to concerns over reduced subject depth and staff reductions. The university has a strong research reputation, with the second-largest research expenditure in Australia and a high number of research students. It is consistently ranked among the top universities in Australia and globally, with a top 30 position in the 2025 U.S. News & World Report rankings and a top 20 position in the 2026 QS World University Rankings.
The University of Melbourne has a rich academic and cultural heritage, with notable alumni including Julia Gillard, Peter Singer, and Elizabeth Blackburn. It operates a network of residential colleges and halls of residence, and offers a wide range of student life activities through its student unions and clubs. The university has faced recent controversies, including student protests over investments in Israeli companies and allegations of surveillance of protesters, which led to an investigation by the Victorian Information Commissioner. Despite these challenges, the university continues to expand its infrastructure and academic offerings, with a focus on innovation and international engagement.
